item.title: China's central bank to step up re-lending policy for stock repurchases and increased holdings
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- The People's Bank of China (PBOC), the central bank, said Wednesday it will step up implementation of its re-lending policy for stock repurchases and increased holdings to maintain capital market stability. Starting Wednesday, the interest rate on the re-lending facility will be lowered by 25 basis points to 1 percent, the PBOC said in a statement. The facility is available to 21 national banks and five systemically important city commercial banks. It covers 100 percent of eligible loans, has a term of one year and can be extended according to the banks' needs. ■

item.title: 7th World Media Summit to kick off in Beijing to boost media cooperation in intelligent age
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
BEIJING, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- The 7th World Media Summit, which is co-hosted by Xinhua News Agency and the People's Government of Beijing Municipality, is to be held from Nov. 5 to 9 in Beijing. According to the summit secretariat, under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action", the summit will bring together nearly 500 delegates from nearly 330 mainstream media outlets, think tanks, government departments and international organizations from 112 countries and regions around the world. Delegates will exchange views on topics including "AI for all and the transformation of global media," "media dialogue and cooperation for a safer world," "AI-enabled communication for expanding exchanges among civilizations," "AI+ and the future of global communication governance" and "the Beijing approach: decoding Chinese modernization." They will also tour Beijing on the sidelines of the summit. The mechanism of the World Media Summit was initiated in 2009 and is an important global platform for high-end media exchange and cooperation. ■

item.title: China willing to work with parties for fruitful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting: top diplomat
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, and Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao co-chair the 37th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Ministerial Meeting via video conference in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu) BEIJING, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- China is willing to work with all parties to do a good job in the final stage of the 2026 APEC "China Year" and contribute to the fruitful results at the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi said on Tuesday. The upcoming leaders' meeting is an important one concerning the future development of the Asia-Pacific region, Wang said when co-chairing the 37th APEC Ministerial Meeting via video conference with Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao. China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China in November this year, which will mark the country's third hosting of the event following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. The theme of this year's summit is "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," while China has identified openness, innovation and cooperation as the three priority areas for this year's APEC cooperation. More than 300 meetings and events have been successfully held during the APEC "China Year," producing a series of cooperation outcomes, said Wang Yi, who is also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee. Expressing readiness to work with all members to make solid and substantive progress in building an Asia-Pacific community, he called on members to uphold mutual respect, deepen solidarity, foster an open environment and sustain the momentum of integration. He said all members should jointly build an innovation ecosystem to cultivate new growth drivers, and expand pathways for cooperation and achieve sustainable development. APEC parties should continue to contribute practical and effective "Asia-Pacific solutions" to the development of the Asia-Pacific region and the world at large, Commerce Minister Wang Wentao said. He noted the international situation is fraught with changes and turmoil, risks of fragmentation in industrial and supply chains are mounting, and the world economy is growing sluggishly. He called on all APEC parties to uphold free trade and innovation-driven development, foster a vibrant engine for growth, advance discussions and policy coordination on digital and intelligent economic and trade rules, and build a fair and equitable international economic and trade order. China will always stay committed to promoting high-level opening up, fully implementing national treatment for foreign-funded enterprises, and encouraging the open-source development and cooperation of new technologies such as artificial intelligence, the commerce minister noted. Representatives of APEC economies and other participants commended the progress of cooperation in various fields and the extensive consensus reached by all parties during the APEC "China Year", expressing their willingness to work with China for the success of the leaders' meeting. ■ Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, and Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao co-chair the 37th Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Ministerial Meeting via video conference in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 3, 2026. (Xinhua/Tian Yu)

item.title: World Internet Conference Wuzhen Summit opens with shared vision of open, inclusive AI
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
HANGZHOU, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- As open-source technologies took center stage at the 2026 World Internet Conference (WIC) Wuzhen Summit that opened on Tuesday, guests called for open collaboration on artificial intelligence (AI) and shared innovation in cyberspace. Held in Wuzhen, east China's Zhejiang Province, the summit gathered about 1,800 delegates from 138 countries and regions, under the theme "Open Source and Openness, Joint Contribution and Shared Benefits -- Jointly Building a Community with a Shared Future in Cyberspace." Addressing the opening ceremony of the summit, Chinese Premier Li Qiang called for joint efforts to build a community with a shared future in cyberspace. "China will continue to pursue open innovation, promote technology transfer and knowledge sharing, and work with all to build an open, inclusive and dynamic global ecosystem for digital innovation," Li said. In her remarks during the ceremony, Yolanda Diaz Perez, Spanish second deputy prime minister and minister for labor and social economy, said the Wuzhen Summit "showcases a way of common governance" and that "AI should serve and deliver well-being for human beings." "What we want is open-source and inclusive AI," she said. "Everyone should have access to the benefits brought by AI." "Together, we can ensure that the next era of technological transformation serves all humanity," Li Junhua, United Nations under-secretary-general for economic and social affairs, told attendees. He also called for turning openness from principle into practice and tangible results. First held in 2014, the Wuzhen Summit brings together government officials, representatives of international organizations, technology executives and researchers to discuss the development and governance of the internet. Openness in action is on display at the Open Source Ecosystem Experience Pavilion, which opened Sunday in Wuzhen, featuring AI open-source achievements, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Zhejiang Lab's 021 Science Foundation Model, alongside AI-related pilot verification cases. Open-source AI has a measurable economic impact. It has the potential to narrow the income gap between developed and developing economies, with open-source models serving as the key driver, according to Justin Yifu Lin, dean of the Institute of New Structural Economics at Peking University, earlier in September. That potential is already translating into practice. In Uganda, former Google scientist Ernest Mwebaze used Alibaba's open-source model Qwen to develop Sunflower, an AI system giving farmers weather and farming advice in local languages. Mwebaze chose Qwen for its better Ugandan-language handling, lower cost and easier customization. That collaborative spirit was shared by industry leaders at the summit. Calling for a future "open by default, trusted by design, and inclusive by nature," John Hoffman, chairman and director of the GSMA Ltd., highlighted a vision for open collaboration. "Openness is strength, not weakness," observed Nii Narku Quaynor, chairman of Ghana Dot Com, a Ghanaian IT company. The summit is also serving as a platform to recognize top-tier global research. A total of 20 projects from around the world were honored with the WIC 2026 Awards for Pioneering Science and Technology in recognition of their breakthroughs in frontier digital technologies on Monday. In a sign of a more collaborative ecosystem, international submissions for the award grew 21 percent year on year, with 18 countries and regions participating for the first time, and the review committee of the award received over 430 submissions from 43 countries and regions this year, according to the WIC. Openness and shared innovation will remain the central theme as the summit runs through Thursday. The WIC was established as an international organization headquartered in Beijing in 2022. ■

item.title: Hainan FTP law implementation yields positive results: report
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
BEIJING, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- The implementation of the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP) Law has yielded positive results, with island-wide special customs operations progressing steadily, according to a law enforcement inspection report submitted to the 25th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC) on Tuesday. The report, from an inspection team of the NPC Standing Committee, said the Hainan FTP's role in promoting opening up and cooperation has become increasingly evident, with its demonstration effect continuing to grow. Hainan FTP's law-based environment has continued to improve, with a preliminary policy and institutional framework in place, according to the report. South China's island province of Hainan formulated a special plan for supporting regulations for the Hainan Free Trade Port Law for the 2021-2025 period and introduced 60 regulations, including those related to intellectual property protection and fair competition. The province has established a free trade port intellectual property court and an international commercial dispute resolution center, advanced reforms in ad hoc arbitration and commercial mediation, and put in place a one-stop, diversified dispute resolution mechanism integrating mediation, arbitration and litigation. The report noted that difficulties and problems remain in implementing the law and the mechanisms for trade liberalization and facilitation. To further advance the implementation of the law, it proposed recommendations in four areas, including improving the policy and institutional framework, further unlocking the benefits of fiscal and tax reforms, optimizing the development environment, and strengthening institutional safeguards. In June 2021, China adopted the Hainan Free Trade Port Law, which stipulates that the development of the port should focus on trade and investment liberalization and facilitation, be supported by the free, orderly, safe and convenient cross-border flows of various factors of production and a modern industrial system, and be underpinned by special tax arrangements, an efficient social governance system and a comprehensive system for the rule of law. On Dec. 18, 2025, China launched island-wide special customs operations in the Hainan Free Trade Port, expanding the share of tariff lines eligible for zero-tariff treatment on qualifying imports from 21 percent to 74 percent. Goods shipped onward from Hainan to the Chinese mainland remain subject to separate customs controls. ■

item.title: New guardians carry forward age-old dialogue in China's Dunhuang
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
* The 9th Silk Road (Dunhuang) International Cultural Expo opened in Dunhuang on Tuesday, gathering around 1,200 delegates from home and abroad with a focus on cultural exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations. * Conservation technologies developed in Dunhuang have been rolled out to more than 150 heritage sites across China, and introduced to other countries including Kyrgyzstan and Myanmar. * While heritage guardians tend to Dunhuang's ancient roots, creative innovators breathe new life into its timeless culture. LANZHOU, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- Dunhuang, famed for its Mogao Caves, was a meeting place for diverse cultures along the ancient Silk Road. Today, it still draws people from far and wide, attracted by its renewed charm. The 9th Silk Road (Dunhuang) International Cultural Expo opened in Dunhuang on Tuesday, gathering around 1,200 delegates from home and abroad with a focus on cultural exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations. Yet the tales of cultural convergence stretch far beyond the expo's forums and exhibition halls, reaching into the daily rhythm of this oasis city, located in northwest China's Gansu Province. For many, Dunhuang is not merely a tourist attraction, but a second home where they build careers inspired by its age-old heritage. They, in turn, inject new energy into heritage preservation and cross-cultural exchange. Some foreign guests at the expo remarked after touring the city that Dunhuang itself stands as a living example of dialogue between different cultures. Zoey Ashlyn Koehl, a student from Oklahoma City University in the United States, was impressed by the welcoming and dynamic vibe of Dunhuang: "I think it's a city open to all different kinds of people to come." SAFEGUARDING HERITAGE Wu Shaoxia adjusted her equipment inside a cave as morning sunlight spilled over the cliff faces of the Mogao Caves. As a cultural relics photographer, she has been based in Dunhuang for 11 years. Now 35 and originally from Shaanxi Province, also in northwest China, Wu is part of the Dunhuang Academy's digital team, featuring many young members from across China. Wu regularly works inside the dim caves, repeating high-precision image capturing endeavors. Notably, she believes that "conservation is not only about rescuing endangered relics, but also racing against time to pass on the millennia-old beauty to future generations." The young cultural workers in Dunhuang carry forward a mission begun decades ago. Over 80 years ago, a batch of heritage workers trekked into the Gobi Desert in a grottoes' conservation and research quest. While their forerunners initially cleared sand from caves by hand and restored relics with simple tools, later generations have witnessed the evolution of conservation approaches. So far, the academy has completed high-precision digital documentation of 323 caves, while its online digital library reunites Dunhuang manuscripts scattered around the world. Notably, as part of the Mogao Caves visitor experience, a dome film that immerses viewers as if inside the real grottoes draws on the academy's digital records. Conservation technologies developed in Dunhuang have been rolled out to more than 150 heritage sites across China, and introduced to other countries including Kyrgyzstan and Myanmar. "Earlier generations safeguarded the physical grottoes. We strive to preserve the look of this 1,000-year-old treasure," said Wu. REIMAGINING TRADITIONS While heritage guardians tend to Dunhuang's ancient roots, creative innovators breathe new life into its timeless culture. Chen Lisong first visited Dunhuang ten years ago, instantly captivated by the depth of its ancient history. Previously based in Shanghai in east China, she relocated to Dunhuang the following year and opened a souvenir shop. The designs of her products draw on iconic Mogao motifs, including the nine-colored deer and flying apsaras. Chen later developed a Silk Road-themed dining space, where visitors can taste signature dishes from different regions along the ancient trade route. For her, Dunhuang culture is not limited to cave murals. It can be woven into dining, accommodation and travel experiences. "Through modern design, it can be transformed into items people can take home," she said. Shen Hongjie, a wood-carving artist, moved from central China's Hunan Province to Dunhuang in 2004, attracted by murals in the Mogao Caves and the local desert landscapes. He set up a studio, blending oil painting and traditional Chinese painting techniques with wood carving to recreate classic Mogao imagery. In the early years of his venture, Dunhuang's cultural tourism sector remained nascent, with limited sales channels for his artworks. As local cultural tourism flourished in recent years, more visitors have poured into Shen's studio, while young apprentices have traveled from afar to learn the craft. Dunhuang received some 24.39 million visitors in 2025, 3.7 times the number recorded in 2020. Cultural and creative products, immersive experiences and intangible heritage workshops are flourishing, appealing to culture-craving young Chinese. BRIDGING CONTINENTS Among those who fell for Dunhuang's charm are some cultural enthusiasts from overseas. Ukrainian dancer Romanovych Inna and Georgian dancer Vaja Bukia settled in Dunhuang in 2024, and have performed in the dance drama "Ancient Sound of Dunhuang." Discovering parallels between Georgian traditional dance and ancient Central Asian whirling dance movements depicted in Dunhuang's murals, Bukia incorporated his native dance elements into the show. "Both Georgia and Dunhuang carry ancient civilizations passed down for generations," he said. For American researcher Neil Schmid, the first full-time foreign scholar at the Dunhuang Academy, his connection with Dunhuang began in the 1980s after reading a book on it. He joined the academy in 2018 and has since shared Dunhuang's heritage globally via lectures, documentaries and publications. "The amazing thing about Dunhuang materials is that there is such a wealth," said Schmid. The ongoing Dunhuang expo, first launched in 2016, further expands such exchanges. Referring to the ancient legacy of Dunhuang, Daren Tang, director-general of the World Intellectual Property Organization, said at the expo: "It reminds us that culture does not grow in isolation, but through exchange, new ideas and creativity." Attending the expo for the second time, Hasebe Tsuyoshi, a professor from Japan's Kansai University who has been studying ancient Dunhuang music scores, said both the ancient and modern Dunhuang are crossroads of world cultures. "Different civilizations have interwoven with one another since ancient times," he said, adding that it is important to continue such exchange and interaction. (Video reporters: Zhang Zhimin and Zhao Tianlin; Video editors: Li Ziwei, Zhang Mocheng and Hong Liang) ■

item.title: Global partners share biodiversity, green development views in giant panda hometown
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
The Global Panda Partners Conference 2026 is launched in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province, Nov. 3, 2026. The main forum of the Global Panda Partners Conference 2026 opened on Tuesday in southwest China's Sichuan Province, known as the "hometown of giant pandas," drawing experts and scholars from over 30 countries and regions. Under the theme of protecting giant panda habitats, building a beautiful world and sharing open opportunities, the event, being held in Chengdu, the provincial capital, has gathered global guests to discuss biodiversity conservation and green development cooperation. (Xinhua/Xu Bingjie) CHENGDU, Nov. 3 (Xinhua) -- The main forum of the Global Panda Partners Conference 2026 opened on Tuesday in southwest China's Sichuan Province, known as the "hometown of giant pandas," drawing experts and scholars from over 30 countries and regions. Under the theme of protecting giant panda habitats, building a beautiful world and sharing open opportunities, the event, being held in Chengdu, the provincial capital, has gathered global guests to discuss biodiversity conservation and green development cooperation. The main forum also saw the release of a think tank report centered on China's green development path. In her speech, Shi Xiaolin, the province's governor, said Sichuan serves as a vital water conservation zone in the upper reaches of the Yangtze River, a key replenishment area in the upper reaches of the Yellow River, and a globally significant region for biodiversity conservation. The province is firmly committed to the path of giving priority to ecological conservation and pursuing green development, she added. Lyu Yansong, editor-in-chief of Xinhua News Agency, said giant pandas are China's national treasure and a shared wealth of all humanity. He noted that the Global Panda Partners Conference is striving to become an important bond for gathering global wisdom and jointly protecting the planet, while continuously expanding the circle of friends of "panda partners." According to Li Yunqing, deputy head of the National Forestry and Grassland Administration, the captive population of giant pandas in China has reached 830, while the genetic diversity of the population continues to improve. Noting that this year marks the 30th anniversary of international scientific research cooperation on giant pandas, the official said that China has cooperated with 26 institutions in 20 countries, resulting in 69 giant pandas living overseas and 73 cubs successfully bred, while the species has drawn over 1 billion visits worldwide. Shahbaz Khan, director of the UNESCO Regional Office for East Asia, said the giant panda inspires affection across languages and generations, and protecting this remarkable animal means caring for the living systems that sustain many other species and support human well-being. China's establishment of the Giant Panda National Park in 2021 has provided an important framework for conservation across the provinces of Sichuan, Shaanxi and Gansu. Work to restore habitats, reconnect ecological corridors and strengthen coordinated management offers valuable experience in protecting ecosystems across administrative boundaries, he noted. "UNESCO looks forward to continued dialogue with Chinese and international partners on safeguarding natural heritage," the director said. Running from Monday to Wednesday, the conference features a main forum, multiple parallel sessions, and other supporting activities centered on international cooperation in giant panda conservation, cultural tourism and other topics. This marks the third edition of the conference. The inaugural conference was held in November 2024 in Chengdu with the theme "Harmonious Coexistence Between Man and Nature." This year's event is co-hosted by the Brand Work Office of Xinhua News Agency, the agency's Sichuan branch, its news and information center, China Wildlife Conservation Association, China Conservation and Research Center for the Giant Panda, and Chengdu Media Group. Sichuan has the largest panda habitat in the world and is home to over 70 percent of China's wild giant panda population. Giant panda conservation serves as a microcosm of China's endeavors to advance ecological civilization. Thanks to sustained conservation efforts, the International Union for Conservation of Nature in 2016 downgraded the giant panda's status from endangered to vulnerable. ■ This photo shows copies of a report centered on China's green development path, which is released during the main forum of the Global Panda Partners Conference 2026 in Chengdu, southwest China's Sichuan Province. item.title: From ancient wisdom to modern engineering: How China manages the Yellow River
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-03
From an ancient vision to modern engineering, China is using precisely controlled water and sediment regulation to tackle sediment buildup in its mother river, the Yellow River. Through 33 coordinated reservoir operations, the average riverbed elevation of the main channel in the lower reaches has been reduced by 3.1 meters, helping improve the river's long-term health and flood prevention.■

item.title: Xi Focus: CPC charts course for tougher action against corruption, stronger self-governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- As China enters a critical period in its modernization drive, the ruling Communist Party of China (CPC) has charted the course for tougher action against corruption and stronger self-governance in the years ahead. Last week, the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee adopted a resolution on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, underscoring the need to step up the fight against corruption and strengthen checks on and oversight over the exercise of power. In doing so, the CPC, the largest political party in the world with more than 100 million members, is seeking to overcome the unique challenges facing a party of its size. These challenges, as outlined by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, include how to maintain the Party's strong governance and leadership capacity, and sustain a clean and upright political environment. "It is now both imperative and timely for the Party to study issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous self-governance," Xi said in a January meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee that set the agenda of the plenum. IMPERATIVE THEME At the January meeting, Xi said the decision to focus the plenary session on Party self-governance had been made after thorough deliberation. Since it was founded in 1921, the Party has attached great importance to its self-supervision and self-governance. Today, the CPC's membership and ranks of officials have undergone structural changes, presenting new challenges for Party building. In response to these challenges, Xi has repeatedly stressed the need for an unwavering commitment to strict Party self-governance, sending a clear signal that discipline will be enforced ever more strictly. "It was with this in mind that the CPC Central Committee decided to make persevering with full and rigorous self-governance the plenum's agenda," he noted. Explaining the resolution at the plenary session, Xi emphasized that persevering with full and rigorous self-governance is essential for maintaining the Party's advanced nature and integrity and consolidating its long-term governing position. This year marks the beginning of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), a critical period for achieving the goal of basically realizing socialist modernization by 2035. "To successfully achieve the goals and tasks of the 15th Five-Year Plan, it is imperative to focus on enhancing the ability and competence of the Party in leading economic and social development," Xi told senior provincial- and ministerial-level officials attending a study session at the Party School of the CPC Central Committee earlier this year. HOW RESOLUTION TAKES SHAPE In January 2026, a drafting group was set up to prepare the resolution, with Xi at its helm. Throughout the drafting process, he played a decisive role, chairing multiple meetings, delivering important speeches and issuing instructions to guide the work. On Feb. 6, Xi chaired the group's first plenary meeting, where he outlined the key principles for the drafting of the resolution. He called for strict measures to address misconduct and corruption, while stressing that Party building should be pursued as a coordinated whole and integrated with the country's broader development goals. At the same meeting, Xi identified 39 key issues for further study, covering the full scope of Party building and governance. On May 6, Xi chaired a meeting in Shanghai on persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, setting out further requirements for the drafting of the resolution. He called for a problem-oriented approach, stressing the need for firm action to tackle prominent problems. As the preparation of the document was underway, Xi stressed the importance of broad consultation and drawing on a wide range of views. He called on non-CPC parties and personages without party affiliation to speak candidly and offer constructive suggestions. During consultation on the draft resolution, 1,173 suggestions for revisions were received from localities, departments and various sectors. After careful consideration, the drafting group incorporated 208 suggestions. The document took shape over more than eight months, with the drafting group holding five plenary meetings and 35 specialized meetings. During the plenary session last week, participants held in-depth discussions and exchanged views, putting forward suggestions that led to 13 revisions to the draft resolution before it was finally adopted on Oct. 29. WHY RESOLUTION MATTERS The resolution examines new circumstances, challenges and tasks facing the Party as it advances full and rigorous Party self-governance. It identifies three increasingly arduous tasks for the CPC: safeguarding China's sovereignty, security and development interests amid a changing international environment; advancing reform and development while maintaining social harmony and stability at home; and preserving the Party's advanced nature and integrity. It also warns that, under new circumstances marked by profound changes, the Party faces challenges to its governance and leadership capacity, the quality of its membership, and its resistance against corruption and moral decline. The resolution has established a problem-oriented approach as one of the guiding principles for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance. It places particular emphasis on strengthening Party spirit among CPC members, as problems in Party conduct and discipline often stem from a lack of strong Party spirit. The resolution sets out specific measures to ensure that Party members and officials remain loyal, upright, and responsible. Another focus is eliminating hidden rules and curbing malpractices such as cultivating connections and making back-room deals. The resolution sets out concrete measures to root out such practices. The more than 200 measures outlined in the resolution combine the reinforcement of existing requirements with new responses to emerging challenges. In the fight against corruption, for example, the resolution calls for intensified efforts to expose new and concealed forms of graft. These include the use of proxies, or so-called "white gloves," to disguise illicit dealings, as well as the "revolving door" phenomenon of bureaucrat-merchant collusion after officials' retirement. It also calls for a crackdown on corruption involving the internet, virtual currencies, cross-border capital flows and blockchain technology. The resolution also sets out measures to improve the Party and state oversight systems and ensure that political responsibility for full and rigorous Party self-governance is effectively discharged. "No other political party in the world takes its own development as seriously as the CPC does, or advances its own self-reform with such a high degree of self-awareness, scientific rigor and systematic effort," Xi has said. "This is a distinctive strength of our Party." The resolution, as observers point out, signals a renewed commitment by the CPC to advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance with higher standards and more concrete measures, recognizing this as a fundamental underpinning of the broader endeavor to build China into a strong country and advance national rejuvenation. "We have already forged a bright path ahead, and we must keep moving forward," Xi has said. ■
